name: Grana

attributes.attribute: drugged the Fianna and eloped with Diarmait
fled with Diarmait toward the Shannon
slept in the Wood of the Two Tents under pursuit
bound by a geis never to hunt boar
name hides the word for sun

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Gráinne is the fiery heroine of the Irish Fenian Cycle. She drugged the whole Fianna, sparing only the man she wanted, and then convinced Diarmait to elope. The couple fled toward the Shannon and slept in the Wood of the Two Tents, since Diarmait feared to share a tent while Fionn chased them. Across Ireland the roadside dolmens are called the beds of Diarmait and Gráinne. Fionn took revenge by luring Diarmait into a boar hunt on Ben Bulben. The hero was under a geis never to hunt boar. The enchanted boar Gulben died, but a sharp bristle stabbed Diarmait and his blood would not stop. Fionn brought water only to let it trickle away. Because her name hides the word for sun, Gráinne is often read as a sun goddess.

okr.objective: Convey Gráinne's elopement with Diarmait, the boar hunt on Ben Bulben, and her sun link.
key_results: Gráinne drugged the Fianna and persuaded Diarmait to elope.
The lovers slept in the Wood of the Two Tents while Fionn pursued.
Fionn lured Diarmait into a forbidden boar hunt on Ben Bulben.
Gráinne's name hides the word for sun, marking her as a sun goddess.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore, 2003
